title: Diagonal evaluation against the shifted normal determinant
statement: Let S be a quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] scheme, let f:X\to S be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and smooth of relative dimension d≥0 [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let R:D_QCoh(O_X)\to D_QCoh(O_S) be a functor whose composition with the full-subcategory inclusion is isomorphic to the restriction of derived direct image Rf_* [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and let a be its specified right adjoint. Let O be an object in D_QCoh(O_S) whose underlying object is isomorphic to the structure sheaf in degree zero [def-pc-derived-category]. Put M=Ω¹_{X/S} [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and M^dual=Hom_{O_X}(M,O_X), the internal sheaf Hom. Then in the recorded derived tensor category [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] there is an isomorphism a(O)\otimes^L (\bigwedge^d M^dual)[-d]\cong O_X[0], where the exterior power is the sheafification of sectionwise exterior powers [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. The derived categories for X and S may be chosen in different universes.

proof.text: Since f is proper it is of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so X is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; the projection \operatorname{pr}_2:X\times_S X\to X is the base change of f, hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and of finite type, so X\times_S X is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] again. Apply the Noetherian derived-direct-image right-adjoint statement [lem-pc-noetherian-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint] to f:X\to S and to the diagonal \Delta:X\to X\times_S X. It gives right adjoints a to Rf_* and c to R\Delta_* on quasi-coherent derived categories.

Because f is smooth of relative dimension d and has closed diagonal, the diagonal \Delta is a Koszul-regular immersion of codimension d; in particular \Delta is perfect, and it is proper because X,S are Noetherian.

The morphism f is flat, being smooth [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The counit/evaluation identity for the diagonal gives \mathcal O_X = c(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*a(\mathcal O_S)) for the flat proper morphism f, by the canonical identity of Tag 0E2Q.

For the perfect proper immersion \Delta, the projection formula identifies c(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*K) with L\Delta^*L\operatorname{pr}_1^*K \mathbin{\otimes^L} c(\mathcal O_{X\times_S X}) for every quasi-coherent complex K, by Tag 0A9U.
For a Koszul-regular immersion of codimension d, the diagonal dualizing object is c(\mathcal O_{X\times_S X}) = \bigwedge^d N_\Delta[-d], by Tag 0BR0.
The conormal sheaf C_\Delta of the diagonal is canonically C_\Delta\cong\Omega^1_{X/S}, by Tag 08S2.

Use the identity Δ ≫ pr₁ = id to identify LΔ* Lpr₁* a(O_S) with a(O_S). The diagonal conormal is Ω¹_{X/S} by Step 6 and is finite locally free of rank d by [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free]. The normal sheaf is its internal dual, so the locally ranked object of the Koszul-dual theorem is the single sheaf wedge^d Hom(Ω¹_{X/S},O_X), shifted by -d. Transport the preceding evaluation chain along these isomorphisms and identify O_X[0] with the derived tensor unit. For the specified R, comparison gives an isomorphism to the canonical full-subcategory lift, and uniqueness of right adjoints transports its adjunction to the specified a; hO transports the input structure object. If the derived universes differ, transport through the unique equivalences of derived localizations before applying the same-universe diagonal lemmas. This yields a(O_S) tensor the shifted normal determinant isomorphic to the unit; no determinant cancellation is used.

mathlib_searches.results: Sheaf pushforward adjunctions, including Scheme.Modules.instIsRightAdjointPushforward; none addresses the derived diagonal determinant evaluation.

mathlib_searches.query: top exterior power of dual of finite locally free sheaf tensor top exterior power is structure sheaf, derived shifts cancel
mathlib_searches.results: ModuleCat.exteriorPower.iso₀ and iso₁ and sheaf free-object identities; no derived sheaf determinant evaluation.

Mathlib results are unrelated uses of dualizing; direct source search finds exteriorPower.pairingDual in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Pairing.lean. It is a ring-module pairing, not a shifted derived sheaf isomorphism.
